Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or
on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the
Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at
the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear
public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Housing
Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or
unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate
and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual
  Commissioners.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the
agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons
with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the
City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this
agenda after it has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.,
every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Bethani Cardenas at ext. 5588 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: PUBLIC HEARING - RESOLUTION NO. NHA-176 ADOPTING PUBLIC
  HOUSING AGENCY ANNUAL PLAN FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027

Background:

Housing authorities are required to complete a five-year Public Housing Agency (PHA) Plan and
an annual plan. These plans inform the United States Department of Housing and Urban
Development (HUD), housing authority participants, and the public about the housing authority’s
mission to serve low-income families. The most recent five-year plan for the Norwalk Housing
Authority (NHA) was adopted in 2025.

The plan presented is the annual plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026/27. The plan has been prepared
on HUD’s standardized template. The PHA Plan requirements have greatly streamlined
reporting for Section 8-only and high-performing housing authorities. HUD annually assigns a
high, standard, or poor performance rating based on evaluation of 14 key indicators under the
Section 8 Management Assessment Program (SEMAP). Since the NHA is a high-performing,
Section 8-only housing authority, the NHA only needs to report whether any Plan elements have
changed since the last Annual Plan submission, any new initiatives, and progress toward
meeting the goals described in the 5-Year PHA Plan.

The annual plan for FY 2026/27 contains the same program and goals as the previous year,
including:
  •  Expand the supply of Assisted Housing
  •  Improve the Quality of Assisted Housing
  •  Maximize leasing and budget utilization
  •  Increase Assisted Housing Choices

  •  Undertaking affirmative measures to provide a suitable living environment for families
  living in assisted housing regardless of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, and

HUD requires that the public have 45 days to review and comment on the plan. The draft plan
was available for review starting March 2, 2026, all public comments due by April 17, 2026.

Fiscal Impact:

There will be no fiscal impact to the General Fund. The Norwalk Housing Authority is funded
solely by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development.

A notice was published in the Norwalk Patriot on February 27, 2026, announcing the availability
of the plan for public review and comment, as well as the date for the public hearing on April 21,
2026. The final plan is due to HUD by April 17, 2026.

Purpose. The 5-Year and Annual PHA Plans provide a ready source for interested parties to locate basic PHA policies, rules, and
requirements concerning the PHA’s operations, programs, and services, including changes to these policies, and informs HUD, families
served by the PHA, and members of the public of the PHA’s mission, goals and objectives for serving the needs of low- income, very low-
income, and extremely low- income families

Applicability. The Form HUD-50075-HCV is to be completed annually by HCV-Only PHAs. PHAs that meet the definition of a Standard
PHA, Troubled PHA, High Performer PHA, Small PHA, or Qualified PHA do not need to submit this form. Where applicable, separate Annual
PHA Plan forms are available for each of these types of PHAs.

Definitions.

(1) High-Performer PHA – A PHA that owns or manages more than 550 combined public housing units and housing choice vouchers, and was
  designated as a high performer on both the most recent Public Housing Assessment System (PHAS) and Section Eight Management
  Assessment Program (SEMAP) assessments if administering both programs, or PHAS if only administering public housing.
(2)  Small PHA - A PHA that is not designated as PHAS or SEMAP troubled, that owns or manages less than 250 public housing units and any
  number of vouchers where the total combined units exceed 550.
(3)  Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Only PHA - A PHA that administers more than 550 HCVs, was not designated as troubled in its most recent
  SEMAP assessment, and does not own or manage public housing.
(4)  Standard PHA - A PHA that owns or manages 250 or more public housing units and any number of vouchers where the total combined units
  exceed 550, and that was designated as a standard performer in the most recent PHAS and SEMAP assessments.
(5)  Troubled PHA - A PHA that achieves an overall PHAS or SEMAP score of less than 60 percent.
(6)  Qualified PHA - A PHA with 550 or fewer public housing dwelling units and/or housing choice vouchers combined and is not PHAS or SEMAP
  troubled.

 B.3 During the 2025-2029 5-Year PHA Plan period, the following progress was made during FY
2025-2026:

Goal #1: Expand the Supply of Assisted Housing
Progress: The NHA issued and fully occupied 60 Project-Based Vouchers. Five FYI vouchers
were awarded and issued, and 18 VASH vouchers were awarded.

Goal #2: Improve the Quality of Assisted Housing
Progress: The NHA received a High overall rating for its SEMAP performance in FY 2024/25.

Goal #3: Maximize leasing and budget utilization
Progress: The NHA is currently facing a high-cost rental market, which has led to overutilization of
the budget and a lower leasing rate. The NHA will not issue additional vouchers until the budget
authority is stabilized.

Goal #4: Increase Assisted Housing Choices
Progress:
•  The Norwalk Housing Authority conducts outreach to landlords and encourages them to
participate in the HCV program, and sends vacant listings to the NHA for our HCV participants.
•  The NHA increased the payment standards by 3% over the Small Area Fair Market Rent
(SAFMR)
•  The NHA provided updated lists of known landlords who accept vouchers, extended the
timeframe for securing a unit, offered one-on-one support, and assisted with security deposits if
funds are available.

Goal #5: Promote self-sufficiency and asset development of assisted households
Progress:
•  The Norwalk Housing Authority continued partnerships established with the Southeast Los
Angeles County Private Industry Council – Workforce Investment Board, the La Mirada-Norwalk
School District Health Start program, California Employment Development Department, Cerritos
College, and local and outside employers.
•  Promoted economic self-sufficiency among program participants by administering the Family
Self-Sufficiency (FSS) Program

Goal #6: Affirmatively Promote Fair Housing
Progress: The NHA ensured equal access to housing opportunities for everyone, regardless of
race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, or disability. It prohibited discrimination in
housing rental practices, aiming to reduce residential segregation and create more inclusive
communities.
